findings.fact: PIDFDs setter calls pidref_set_pidfd(), which on EMFILE/ENFILE/ENOMEM duplicating the supplied FD converts it to a numeric-only PidRef. unit_watch_pidref() duplicates it again via pidref_copy(), which independently permits the same downgrade. pidref_verify() returns non-error 0 when fd<0; attach accepts that. No strict-retention flag or retained-PIDFD acknowledgement exists in this selected API. Client no-fallback marshalling does not prohibit manager fallback; even GetUnitByPIDFD uses this conversion.

unit_attach_pids_to_cgroup() calls pidref_verify(), then cg_attach(path,pid). cg_attach writes a decimal PID to cgroup.procs. The source explicitly identifies the verify/write race. On user-manager permission failure another path submits AttachProcessesToUnit(ssau) to the system manager using that numeric PID. Holding a PIDFD in the sender does not make either operation an atomic attachment of that PIDFD identity; reaping/reuse after verification can invalidate it.

For a retained real PIDFD, a reaped original process causes pidfd_get_pid() to return ESRCH at property consumption, or pidref_verify() to fail and skip it at activation. With zero successful attachments scope_enter_running refuses. Exit-before-reap is different: the PIDFD can still resolve to a zombie; Linux migration excludes PF_EXITING tasks and a successful no-op cgroup.procs write can nevertheless be counted by systemd as an attachment. Thus neither a readable PIDFD nor a successful job is by itself the complete workload/empty-scope proof. These deductions are conditional on no manager downgrade/race and are not installed executed controls.

StartTransientUnit creates the transient unit/file before applying PIDFDs, so a rejected dead PIDFD need not mean no unit-state effects. An already queued start can realize its cgroup, acquire InvocationID and export state before finding no PIDs. The StartTransientUnit reply contains a job path only after manager_add_job_full; reply loss or client timeout leaves submission outcome uncertain. CancelJob addresses an already identified job, not a not-yet-replied request serial. Cancel/JobRemoved prove a job outcome, not rollback of unit/cgroup effects or active workload termination.

When the last tracked job client disappears, bus_job_track_handler only considers GC. job_may_gc rejects ordinary scope jobs (gc_jobs is for external-state device units). Scope Controller disappearance merely clears its controller reference, not the scope or queued start. AddRef pins observation lifetime while connected; it is not cancellation. Closing/reaping systemd-run or losing its D-Bus connection is therefore not terminal evidence.

RuntimeMax is ActiveEnterTimestampMonotonic plus the relative duration; JobTimeout is manager job-queue begin plus a relative duration and JobRunningTimeout begins when the job runs. Neither accounts for arbitrary delay before manager receipt/queueing. Job timeout cancels job waiting and does not change the unit itself. Computing a remaining duration in the client, even using the original clock, cannot turn delayed manager application into the original absolute deadline. Existing coordinator post-handoff checks cannot protect a dead or SIGSTOPed pre-admission owner.

already_running_outer_deadline_plus_stri.conditional_workload_result: If an independently enforced, already running original absolute bound kills the sole pre-exec foreground process, it has not spawned candidate children, and the native manager truly retains and uses that exact identity atomically, that dead process cannot later exec the candidate. coherent_findings.fact: After Popen, run() catches only TimeoutExpired around communicate and only ProcessLookupError around killpg; there is no encompassing finalizer. A communicate I/O/decode/control exception or a non-ProcessLookupError during stop escapes without the original process handle, birth or observation. The outer qualify catches BaseException but receives observation={} and does not own that Popen. finish_owner can then produce STOP_UNCONFIRMED without the handle, because qualify copies it only if the earlier exception already carried owned_process. A unit may remain populated; returning STOP_UNCONFIRMED is honest but does not preserve recoverable custody. The only whole-unit callback is on_timeout; control/error exits do not call it. In the inner Containment path, finish() begins with budget.check() outside its StopUnconfirmed conversion, so exhaustion can replace an earlier StopUnconfirmed with ValueError and lose its retained handle.
